name: Rees-Dart Track: Rees Saddle to Dart Hut
why: Up the Rees valley under Mount Earnslaw/Pikirakatahi, over the 1,471 m Rees Saddle and down Snowy Creek to Dart Hut, below the moraines of the Dart Glacier.
book: The full circuit is closed: a large slip between Daleys Flat Hut and Chinamans Bluff has shut the Dart Track indefinitely. DOC's options: in and out of the Rees valley to Dart Hut (this trip), Cascade Saddle to Dart Hut, or a booked helicopter hop with Heli Glenorchy. Book Shelter Rock and Dart huts. Muddy Creek car park is 68 km from Queenstown via Glenorchy.
water: Hut taps are untreated: boil before use. Streams on the way.
dangers: Rivers and side streams flood often, after rain and during snowmelt: carry an emergency shelter and spare food, and wait.
The upper Snowy Creek bridge is removed each winter and may not be back until December: ask the Queenstown visitor centre.
Avalanche paths above the bushline from late autumn to early summer.
Steep drops beside the track below Rees Saddle; Waterfall Creek bridge near Shelter Rock Hut is damaged.
turnaround: If rain is forecast or Rees Saddle is in cloud or snow, stay at Shelter Rock Hut or walk back out.

points.name: Muddy Creek car park
points.note: Farm track over Rees Valley Station (private land, 12 km, 4-5 h) past Lennox Falls to the national park boundary swing bridge.

points.name: Shelter Rock Hut
points.note: Night out and back, 19 km and 6-8 h in, above the bushline on the Rees River.

points.name: Rees Saddle
points.note: 1,471 m, on a lightly marked climb near the bluff. Patrick Caples crossed here in 1864 and was the first European to describe the Dart Glacier.

points.name: Dart Hut
points.note: Over the swing bridge on Snowy Creek, 10 km and 4-6 h from Shelter Rock Hut. The Dart Glacier lies up the valley. Walk back out the same way.
